at_a_glance.expert: Moderate certainty: in expert hands POEM and LHM with Dor give similar swallowing relief to 5 years, and POEM carries a persistent excess of reflux and acid exposure. The serious-complication advantage of POEM rests on low-certainty data, and the subtype advantages on observational data.
at_a_glance.original_quote: In treatment-naive adults, POEM is non-inferior to laparoscopic Heller myotomy with Dor fundoplication for Eckardt-defined success at 2 and 5 years (83.0% vs 81.7%; 75.0% vs 70.8%) and had fewer serious adverse events.
at_a_glance.today: In an expert unit offering both, choose by shared decision on reflux. Favour LHM+Dor when avoiding reflux matters most, and POEM for type III (conditional) or after a failed LHM. A unit early in its POEM series should not assume the trial results apply to it.

points: Inherited belief going into 2021–26: POEM was non-inferior to LHM+Dor for 2-year success (83.0% vs 81.7%, difference 1.4, -8.7 to 11.4) and had fewer serious adverse events (2.7% vs 7.3%), at the price of more oesophagitis (44% vs 29%) [1]. POEM beat a single pneumatic dilation series at 2 years (92% vs 54%) [4]. Pneumatic dilation matched LHM at 2 years (86% vs 90%) [6].

What changed in the latest five years was knowledge, not treatment. No new POEM vs LHM trial was treated in 2021–26, and the table labels this comparison no_recent_data and one_era_only. The new information is long follow-up of older cohorts, plus one trial after failed LHM [8].

What held: 5-year success stayed similar (75.0% vs 70.8%) [2]. Both arms lost ground: POEM by 8.0 points (derived) and LHM by 10.9 points (derived). The reflux trade-off persisted: oesophagitis 41% vs 31%, LA B–D 14% vs 7%, abnormal acid exposure 62% vs 31% [2]. The table labels reflux a persistent_tradeoff, but flags it points_only, so this is an observation argued here, not a computed trend.
Against dilation, POEM's lead held at 5 years (81% vs 40%, adjusted difference 41%, 25 to 57) [5]. LHM and dilation stayed level at 10 years (74% vs 74%) [7].

What will the patient live with over time, and does it persist? Researcher: about three in four have lasting swallowing relief with either operation. The reflux burden after POEM had not faded by 5 years, and PPI use was higher (46% vs 13% against dilation) [2, 5].
debate.speaker: researcher
debate.title: Inherited belief, what changed, what held

points: H1, intrinsic technique trade-off: POEM divides the sphincter with no anti-reflux barrier, while LHM adds a Dor wrap. Test: the excess reflux appears in every comparison with a different design. Oesophagitis was 44% vs 29% at 2 years [1]. Reflux by GerdQ was 64.6% vs 11.1% [3]. Against dilation, oesophagitis was 41% vs 7% [4]. After failed LHM it was 34.3% vs 15%, not significant [8]. The pooled RR for oesophagitis was 3.10 (2.17–4.41) [14]. Consistent.

H2, ascertainment and attrition: pH testing was done in 37% of patients, 20% were lost by 5 years, and the trial was open-label [2]. Endoscopy after POEM vs dilation was done only in patients still in remission [4, 5]. Test: this could change the size of the gap but cannot explain why the direction is the same across all trials.

H3, surgeon experience: the trials were run in expert centres, and the 40-patient trial used one highly experienced POEM operator [3]. Test: this may explain the low serious-event rate after POEM (2.7%) [1]. No data by operator experience exist to test it.

H4, comparator protocol: the dilation arm allowed one series in the POEM trial [5] but a series of dilations in the LHM trial [6, 7]. Test: this fits a dilation result that is far below POEM (40% vs 81%) yet equal to LHM (74% vs 74%).

H5, recency mistaken for reliability: the meta-analyses of 2021–26 re-pool the same randomised trials [9, 10, 11, 13, 14]. Test: the RR of 3.10 [14] adds one propensity-matched cohort to 3 RCTs. It adds few new randomised patients.

H6, case mix and subtype: the trial populations were mostly type II (64.8% in one network) [10]. A type III benefit (observational OR 3.50, 1.39–8.77) [12] could be averaged away. This is untested by randomised data.
Leading explanation: H1 for the persistent reflux gap. H4 is accepted alongside it for the dilation discrepancy.
debate.speaker: researcher
debate.title: Competing explanations tested

points: Against H1: the 5-year endoscopic gap was 10.2 points (-7.0 to 26.8), which is not significant [2]. Reflux symptom scores were similar (1.3 vs 1.1) [2]. One network found no significant POEM vs LHM difference in reflux or oesophagitis [9]. The long-term pool reached significance only after excluding outlier studies [11]. The acid exposure figure of 62% vs 31% rests on 37% of patients [2].

Against the opposite reading, that the reflux gap is an artefact: different trials, comparators and measures all point the same way [1, 3, 4, 8, 14]. Selection bias would have to act in the same direction in every one of them, which is unlikely.

Duplicates: [1] and [2] are one trial, [4] and [5] are one trial, and [6] and [7] are one trial. Direct POEM vs LHM evidence is one multicentre trial plus 40 patients [3]. The newest network meta-analysis likely counts 2-year and 5-year reports as separate trials [13].

Time is confounded with design. The only primary trial treated in 2021–26 studied previously operated patients over 1 year [8], so the latest era cannot test any change in primary POEM vs LHM results.
The 10-year LHM vs dilation result has heavy attrition (40 vs 36 analysed) [7]. Its type II and type III subgroup findings are exploratory.

What will the patient live with over time, and does it persist? Skeptic: what the patient feels may differ less than the endoscopy suggests, since symptom scores were similar [2]. Nothing beyond 5 years is known for POEM, so persistence after that is unmeasured, and so are Barrett's oesophagus and stricture.
debate.speaker: skeptic
debate.title: Attack on H1 and its opposite

points: On H1: not reaching significance at 5 years with 20% attrition is a power problem. LA B–D oesophagitis still doubled (14% vs 7%) [2], and pH testing showed a 31.7-point excess (9.8 to 50.5) even in the tested subset [2].
Similar symptom scores do not settle the matter. Acid exposure without symptoms still needs PPI and surveillance, and POEM needed more PPI against dilation (46% vs 13%) [5].
Possible convergence: LHM+Dor oesophagitis rose from 29% to 31% between 2 and 5 years [1, 2]. A slowly loosening wrap could narrow the gap over time (own inference, unresolved).

On H3: the trial was not run early on the learning curve, so the owner's concern runs the other way here. The trial may show the best a unit can achieve rather than hide a signal. An expert-centre result supports POEM for expert operators only.
On the next study: the predictive range for a new trial of 2-year success is 1.4 points (-8.65 to 11.45) in the table. Parity in success is the expected result, not a certainty.

What will the patient live with over time, and does it persist? Researcher: swallowing relief persists to 5 years in about three quarters of patients with either operation. The reflux cost of POEM persists to 5 years on pH and endoscopy. The patient should weigh a lower serious-complication rate up front against the long-term reflux.
debate.speaker: researcher
debate.title: Reply

points: H1, intrinsic trade-off: hold. The decisive study is the 5-year report of the multicentre trial [2]. It persists in direction, but its size is uncertain because pH testing was incomplete.
H2, ascertainment and attrition: partial. It weakens the size of the gap, not its direction. Decisive: [2] (37% pH tested) and [5] (remission-only endoscopy).
H3, surgeon experience: unresolved. No outcome-by-operator data exist. Decisive: [3], with a single expert operator, which limits transfer to less experienced units.
H4, dilation protocol: hold. Decisive: [5] against [7].
H5, re-pooled meta-analyses mistaken for new evidence: concede. The researcher accepts that the 2021–26 pools add almost no new randomised POEM vs LHM patients [13, 14].
H6, subtype masking: unresolved. The only support is observational [12], and the conditional guideline rests on it [16].

What will the patient live with over time, and does it persist? Skeptic's close: to 5 years, similar swallowing and more acid after POEM. Beyond 5 years nothing is measured, so neither side can claim the answer.
debate.speaker: skeptic
debate.title: Closing each explanation

decisions.choice: Either POEM or LHM+Dor, by shared decision on the reflux trade-off.
decisions.reason: Success was similar at 2 and 5 years (75.0% vs 70.8%). POEM had fewer serious adverse events (2.7% vs 7.3%) but more acid exposure (62% vs 31%) [1, 2].
decisions.scenario: Routine treatment-naive type II achalasia in a unit expert in both operations

decisions.reason: The reflux excess after POEM is consistent across studies (pooled RR for oesophagitis 3.10, abnormal pH 1.94) and persisted at 5 years (LA B–D 14% vs 7%) [2, 14].
decisions.scenario: Patient for whom avoiding reflux or long-term PPI matters most

decisions.choice: POEM favoured, with a plan for reflux surveillance.
decisions.reason: Observational success was 93% vs 71% (OR 3.50) [12], and the guideline recommendation is conditional [16]. No randomised subtype data exist.
Success at 1 year was 62.2% vs 26.7%. Oesophagitis was 34.3% vs 15%, not significant, and follow-up is 1 year only [8].
decisions.scenario: Persistent or recurrent symptoms after LHM

decisions.choice: Pneumatic dilation, given as a series with repeats planned.
decisions.reason: A series of dilations matched LHM at 10 years (74% vs 74%) and did better in type II on exploratory analysis [7]. A single series fell well short of POEM (40% vs 81%) [5].
decisions.scenario: Patient accepting repeat procedures who wants to avoid an operation

decisions.choice: LHM+Dor, or refer for POEM until the unit has built its own outcome record.
decisions.reason: The trial results come from expert centres, one with a single highly experienced operator [1, 3]. Outcomes early in a series are not reported.
decisions.scenario: Surgeon or unit early in a POEM series

decisions.choice: POEM is reasonable, with PPI and endoscopic follow-up planned.
decisions.reason: Non-inferior success to 5 years, shorter procedure time in one trial (95.7 vs 218.75 min), and more PPI use [2, 3, 5].
decisions.scenario: Expert POEM operator, treatment-naive patient who accepts acid suppression

eras.going_in: This evidence set holds no earlier randomised data. The open question was whether pneumatic dilation could match LHM.
eras.knowledge_after: By 2011, a series of dilations was known to match LHM at 2 years. POEM was not yet in this randomised evidence. The 10-year report came later, in 2024. Treatment years are assumed.
eras.showed: One multicentre trial of dilation vs LHM+Dor (n=201): 2-year success 86% vs 90%, perforation 4% with dilation, mucosal tears 12% with LHM [6]. Its 10-year report showed 74% vs 74%, with heavy attrition. Exploratory subgroups found dilation better in type II (p=0.03) and a trend to LHM in type III (p=0.05) [7].

eras.going_in: Dilation was roughly equal to LHM at 2 years [6].
eras.knowledge_after: Unchanged. The early (Idea, Development, Exploration) stages of POEM are not represented in this evidence set.
eras.showed: No primary study in this era.

eras.going_in: Dilation was roughly equal to LHM. There was no randomised POEM data.
eras.knowledge_after: POEM was non-inferior to LHM+Dor for swallowing to 5 years, with a persistent reflux trade-off, and superior to a single dilation series. The results became known between 2019 and 2025, and treatment years are assumed.
eras.showed: Multicentre trial [1], with its 5-year report [2]: 2-year success 83.0% vs 81.7% (difference 1.4, -8.7 to 11.4); serious adverse events 2.7% vs 7.3%; oesophagitis 44% vs 29%. At 5 years: success 75.0% vs 70.8%, oesophagitis 41% vs 31%, acid exposure 62% vs 31% (37% tested), 20% attrition. Single-centre trial of 40 patients: GerdQ reflux 64.6% vs 11.1%, procedure time 95.7 vs 218.75 min [3]. POEM vs dilation trial: success 92% vs 54% at 2 years [4] and 81% vs 40% at 5 years [5]; oesophagitis 41% vs 7%; PPI use 46% vs 13%.

eras.going_in: POEM was non-inferior to LHM+Dor at 2 years with fewer serious adverse events and more oesophagitis [1], and superior to single-series dilation [4].
eras.knowledge_after: The direction is unchanged. The table labels this comparison no_recent_data, and labels reflux a persistent_tradeoff that rests on points only. No new primary POEM vs LHM trial was treated in this era.
eras.showed: One primary trial, treated after failed LHM: POEM 62.2% vs dilation 26.7% at 1 year; oesophagitis 34.3% vs 15%, not significant [8]. Meta-analyses re-pooled earlier trials: success RR 1.09 (0.86–1.39) [10]; success OR 1.43 (0.96–2.13) in mixed designs [11]; oesophagitis RR 3.10 and abnormal pH RR 1.94 [14]. The guideline gave a conditional preference for POEM in type III [16].

board.linked_note: Success and reflux moved together. Both arms lost swallowing success between 2 and 5 years (POEM by 8.0 points, LHM by 10.9 points, both derived), while the reflux gap held: endoscopic oesophagitis 15 then 10 points, acid exposure 31.7 points, and more PPI use [1, 2, 5]. Serious adverse events favoured POEM, but overall adverse events did not differ in pooling [1, 14]. Shorter operative time came from a single expert operator [3]. Dilation success depends on whether repeat dilations count as failure [5, 7]. Same trial, counted once: [1] and [2]; [4] and [5]; [6] and [7]. The meta-analyses [9, 10, 11, 13, 14] re-pool overlapping trials.

opinion.curve_reading: For POEM vs LHM, the evidence is at IDEAL stage 3 (Assessment): one multicentre trial and one 40-patient trial. Five-year follow-up moves it toward stage 4 (Long-term), but nothing beyond 5 years is reported. The trials ran in expert centres, late on their operators' learning curves, so they likely show best-case results rather than hide an early-curve signal. Subtype evidence remains at observational stages [12]. Treatment years are assumed throughout.
opinion.did_not_improve: Reflux after POEM did not improve with time: oesophagitis was 41% and acid exposure 62% at 5 years [2]. Swallowing success fell in both arms between 2 and 5 years [1, 2]. No POEM vs LHM trial was treated in 2021–26, and there are no randomised subtype data. Follow-up beyond 5 years, and data on Barrett's oesophagus or stricture, are missing. Single-series dilation lost ground against POEM by 5 years [5].
opinion.verdict: Moderate certainty: POEM and LHM+Dor give similar swallowing relief to 5 years in expert hands, and POEM carries more reflux and acid exposure that persist to 5 years. Low certainty that POEM has fewer serious adverse events. Very low certainty for subtype advantages. Moderate certainty that POEM beats single-series dilation, both in treatment-naive patients and after failed LHM.
opinion.why: My view: the reflux gap is built into the technique, because POEM leaves no anti-reflux barrier, and it is seen across every comparator [1, 3, 4, 8, 14]. The competing reading is that incomplete pH testing, attrition and open-label assessment exaggerate the gap, since symptom scores were similar and the 5-year endoscopic difference was not significant [2, 9, 11]. The two readings agree on direction and differ on size.

scoreboard.for: Excess reflux in every comparison and design [1, 3, 4, 8, 14]
scoreboard.name: Intrinsic technique trade-off (no anti-reflux barrier after POEM)

scoreboard.against: Cannot explain why the direction is the same across trials
scoreboard.for: pH in 37% of patients, 20% attrition, open-label, remission-only endoscopy [2, 5]
scoreboard.name: Ascertainment, attrition and open-label bias

scoreboard.for: Expert centres; single highly experienced operator in [3]
scoreboard.name: Surgeon experience and learning curve

scoreboard.for: Dilation 40% vs POEM 81% with a single series [5], but 74% vs LHM 74% with a series allowed [7]
scoreboard.name: Dilation protocol and comparator design

scoreboard.against: The newest pool adds one cohort [14]
scoreboard.for: Overlapping pools; probable double-counting of trial reports [13]
scoreboard.name: Recent meta-analyses mistaken for new evidence

scoreboard.against: No randomised subtype analysis; confounded series
scoreboard.for: Mostly type II in trials (64.8%) [10]; observational type III OR 3.50 [12]
scoreboard.name: Case mix and subtype masking a type III benefit

settle: A second independent multicentre randomised trial of POEM vs LHM+Dor, with blinded outcome assessment and complete pH monitoring.
Follow-up beyond 5 years of the multicentre POEM vs LHM cohort [1, 2], with complete endoscopy and pH testing.
A randomised POEM vs LHM trial stratified by subtype, powered for type III.
A randomised trial of an anti-reflux modification of POEM (for example POEM with fundoplication) against LHM+Dor.
A prospective study of POEM outcomes by operator experience, from the start of a series.
A randomised trial of POEM vs on-demand repeated dilation series, with long follow-up.
board.topic: POEM vs laparoscopic Heller myotomy with Dor for idiopathic achalasia, with the place of pneumatic dilation

triggers.if: the next independent randomised trial shows similar success with blinded, complete pH testing and no acid-exposure excess after POEM
triggers.then: H1 is weakened, the reflux trade-off shrinks, and POEM becomes the default in expert units.

triggers.if: follow-up beyond 5 years shows POEM success falling faster than LHM+Dor
triggers.then: Durability favours LHM+Dor, especially in younger patients.

triggers.if: long-term data show Barrett's oesophagus or peptic stricture after POEM
triggers.then: LHM+Dor is favoured for patients with long life expectancy.

triggers.if: a randomised subtype analysis confirms better success with POEM in type III
triggers.then: The conditional type III preference becomes a firm one.

triggers.if: a trial of POEM with an anti-reflux procedure shows reflux close to LHM+Dor
triggers.then: The main trade-off is removed for that technique.

triggers.if: outcome-by-experience data show worse results early in a POEM series
triggers.then: Units early in a series should refer or choose LHM+Dor until they reach proficiency.
